# Coordinate a tax audit or examination

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a tax authority opens a formal examination or requests records beyond routine filing clarification. A controlled response record with adviser-reviewed submissions, tracked findings and authorized resolution.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Preserve the notice and relevant records

agent-runnable


Record the authority, taxpayer, period, scope, response channel and dates stated in the notice. Preserve existing evidence and pause routine disposal for the affected records without changing historical documents.

- Sources: [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Appoint the adviser and agree the response strategy

human · human approval required


Verify the authority contact and have qualified tax counsel or the accountant assess representation, response dates and the scope of information requested. Assign one response owner and resolve privilege or confidentiality questions before disclosure.

- Sources: [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Build a reconciled evidence and request register

agent-runnable


Map requests to returns, ledgers, invoices and supporting workpapers. Identify omissions and discrepancies openly, maintaining source versions and an index of what has been reviewed and supplied.

- Sources: [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve responses and manage authority discussions

human · human approval required


The authorized representative reviews factual explanations and documents before submission. Track follow-up questions and meeting records without admitting disputed conclusions or agreeing adjustments outside approved authority.

- Sources: [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review findings and close or contest the examination

human · human approval required


Have advisers assess proposed changes, response rights and relevant dates for the specific jurisdiction. Obtain authority for a settlement, challenge or amended return and retain the final decision, payments and continuing obligations.

- Verify: A controlled response record with adviser-reviewed submissions, tracked findings and authorized resolution.
- Sources: [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)
